hotel-fb-operate-or-outsource-2026-11-12.title: 酒店餐饮，该自营还是外包
hotel-fb-operate-or-outsource-2026-11-12.titleEn: Hotel Food and Beverage: Operate It, or Outsource It
hotel-fb-operate-or-outsource-2026-11-12.description: 酒店餐饮该自营还是外包，先按早餐、正餐、宴会和员工餐拆开，再看每一块的账记在谁名下、现场抓手在谁手里。本文说明哪类餐段更该留下、哪类可以交出去，以及外包合同里不写就会在厨房失控的事项。
hotel-fb-operate-or-outsource-2026-11-12.descriptionEn: Whether a hotel should operate its food and beverage or outsource it depends on the job each meal period does. Split breakfast, all-day dining, banquets and staff meals before comparing a loss with a quote.
hotel-fb-operate-or-outsource-2026-11-12.author: 迈创兄弟C&T（MarvelBros C&T）
content: 酒店餐饮该自营还是外包，要先看清餐厅在这家店里承担哪几件事，再决定哪一块自己做、哪一块交给别人。把全部餐饮一次性外包，或一次性留在自己手里，往往会把早餐、宴会和员工餐绑在同一个答案上。
常见的错法有两个，方向相反。看见餐厅账面亏损，就认定自营做不下去；拿一份外包报价跟厨房工资总额比一比，就认定外包更省。亏损可能只是早餐收入记在了客房，报价低也可能是能源、设备和客诉赔偿还留在酒店账上。
## 餐厅在这家店里，实际在做哪几件事？
口头上的“餐饮”，现场通常是四件不同的事。住客早餐和简餐跟着客房走，客人拿含早来比价。宴会和会议配餐跟着销售走，菜单和上菜时间要在开席前改得动。对外的餐厅或酒吧，是在问这家店要不要自己养一处客人专程过来的地方。员工餐只保障后场按时吃饭，不直接决定住客满不满意，却会把原料和工时搅进宴会成本。
四块的收入、人手和出错的代价都不一样。早餐可以交给能按点出餐的一方，宴会厨房仍由酒店排班；只把员工餐拆出去、其余不动，也同样说得通。先按功能拆，再谈谁来做。
## 自营留下什么，外包交出去什么？
自营时，菜单、排班和采购还在酒店手里，损耗也在酒店手里。客人投诉到前台，当班的人可以当天改。外包之后，日常抓手换成合同。承包方拿走分成或管理费，酒店少养一套后场，也少了临时改菜单、加人、停售的便利。客人并不读合同。餐厅挂着酒店的名字，食物安全、等候和卫生出了问题，先找上门的是酒店。
下表只对照责任落在谁手里，不用来证明哪一种更赚钱。

| 事项 | 自营时 | 外包时 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 菜单和出品 | 酒店定，当天可以改 | 按合同执行；没写标准，就跟着承包方的习惯走 |
| 人手和采购 | 酒店承担工资、损耗和供应商 | 承包方承担日常人工和进货，酒店失去现场账 |
| 投诉和食物安全 | 酒店处理，证照上的经营者也是酒店 | 客人仍找酒店；追偿、停售和进厨房检查要写进合同 |
| 场地、设备和能源 | 酒店的资产，酒店付 | 谁投资、谁维护、到期归谁，单列，不能混进全包 |
| 跟客房、会议的配合 | 内部可以临时加人 | 靠约定时段、最低人手和违约；临时加会要事先说清 |
## 哪几类店，更该把关键餐段留在自己手里？
客人是冲着吃来的，关键餐段就不要先外包。度假村里那间餐厅、靠本地菜把住客留下来的店、名字已经传出去的餐厅，换一套班子，住客先感知到的是菜和招呼变了。房价能不能守住，是后面的事。
会议和宴会如果是这家店的主要收入，关键厨房也更该留下。销售在方案里答应的分餐、临时加人和改菜单，往往发生在开席前几小时。外包若按固定菜单、固定人手结算，销售每加一场会，都要先问合同里有没有这一项。
还有两种情况不该为了省事交出去。品牌或管理合同已经写明出品、供应商和人员标准，候选承包方做不到，或者不接受酒店进厨房检查，外包只是把达不到标准的风险从班组挪到一份合同上。厨房班组已经稳定，外包省不下人，只是多一层分成，同样没有换人的理由。
## 哪几类店，可以把某一块交出去？
餐饮只是住客配套，酒店又没有稳定的厨师和采购时，早餐或某一个餐段可以交给能按点交付的一方。前提是这一块做不好，原因在出品和排班，而不是它在给客房或会议托底。托底的那一块交出去，房价里的含早和会议方案会一起变差，账上却不一定立刻看出来。
员工餐最适合先从宴会厨房里拆开，收成固定标准的工作餐，或单独交给别人做。它不承载住客体验。继续用宴会的人和原料来做，宴会亏在哪里就一直算不清。
某一块可以外包，要同时看得见三件事：约定的时段和菜单做得到；食品经营许可证有人持有，酒店能抽查；酒店保留停售和更换的权利。缺一件，报价低只说明少付了一笔费用，没有说明风险已经离开这家店。
## 为什么不能只比餐厅亏不亏、报价高不高？
餐厅账面亏损，先归位再判断。早餐已经含在房价里，收入在客房、成本在餐饮，餐厅一定会显示亏损。宴会场地的折旧若记在客房部，厨房的账会更难看。把这些挪回各自的餐段之后，仍然人多、原料损耗高、出餐不稳定，才是自营本身的问题。
外包报价也先拆开。管理费和分成之外，场地、能源、设备维护、员工餐、早餐券怎么结算、宴会有没有保底、淡季留多少人、食物安全事件谁赔偿、合同提前结束时人怎么安置，常常仍由酒店付。拿报价直接跟现在的工资比，会把这些继续发生的支出算成已经省下来的钱。
比较要按同一个餐段做。早餐、正餐、宴会、员工餐分开，每一块写明收入记在哪、人工和原料谁付、能源和设备谁付、客诉和赔偿谁承担。有一块对不上，先不要整包切换。
## 外包合同里，哪几条不写就会在现场失控？
合同要写到厨房当天能执行。“保证品质”四个字执行不了。需要写明的是：出品差到什么程度可以停售；营业时段，以及入住高峰、会议高峰至少留多少人；卫生、证照、保险，食物安全事件里谁先安顿客人、谁赔偿；哪些原料必须走指定供应商；设备属于谁、谁保养、合同结束如何移交；员工跟谁签合同，解除时谁安置；多久结一次账、有没有保底、能源怎么分；酒店能不能进厨房，做到哪一步可以提前解除。
这些条款没有一套可以照抄的数字。保底高低、能源谁出，取决于这一块是住客配套还是对外餐厅。写不进合同的口头承诺，开业之后没有人执行。
自营也不是省掉这张纸就更安全。自营要有人按天看原料进价、每个餐段出了多少、客诉指向的是菜、是等、还是卫生。没有这张日常账，自营只是把亏损留在自己部门的名称下面。
## 决定之前，现有餐厅要先看清哪几件事？
先对五件事。早餐、正餐、宴会、员工餐的收入和直接成本，现在能不能分开记。近期客诉里，有多少指向出品、等候和卫生，有多少其实在说房价。厨师和后场是不是主要只为早餐存在。品牌合同或管理合同有没有限制外包，有没有要求事先书面同意。食品经营许可证在谁名下，厨房设备登记在谁的资产上。
五件里有一件对不上，先补账或先问合同，不要先签外包。已经能分开的那一块，挑一个餐段试运行，看三件：出品稳不稳定，高峰加不加得上人，客诉找谁。这一段过了，再决定其余部分。不要同一天把早餐、宴会和员工餐一起交出去。
试运行若出品不稳、高峰加不上人，或客人仍找酒店而合同里没有停售权，这一餐段就停下来，不把其余餐段一起交出去。停下来不是回到原样就算了，要把没分开的账补上，再决定下一块。
这张表要由两边一起填，不能只听一边。业主决定哪一块留下、哪一块交出，以及保底、能源和提前解除写到什么程度。总经理或餐饮负责人拿出餐段账、班组能不能按点出餐、客诉指向哪里，但不代替业主签字。品牌或管理公司若握着出品标准，外包前先按合同取得书面同意。厨房说亏损，只是信息，不是业主已经批准外包。
迈创兄弟C&T（MarvelBros C&T）可以按一家店现有的餐段、合同和后场，把自营与外包放在同一张表上比。这张表用来看哪一块该留、哪一块可以交，不代替业主做决定。
contentEn: Whether a hotel should operate its food and beverage or outsource it depends on what the restaurant is actually doing in that property. Decide piece by piece. Handing the whole department to a contractor, or keeping all of it in-house, ties breakfast, banquets and staff meals to one answer.

Two mistakes point in opposite directions. A loss on the restaurant account is taken to mean in-house operation has failed. A contractor's quote is compared with the kitchen payroll and taken to mean outsourcing is cheaper. The loss may only mean breakfast revenue sits in rooms. The low quote may leave energy, equipment and guest claims on the hotel's books.
## What is the restaurant actually doing in this hotel?

What people call food and beverage is usually four different jobs. Guest breakfast and light meals travel with the room product; guests compare hotels on whether breakfast is included. Banquet and meeting catering travel with sales; the menu and service times have to be changeable before the event starts. A restaurant or bar open to the public asks whether the hotel should run a place guests come for on purpose. Staff meals only get the back of house fed on time. They do not decide whether a guest is satisfied, but they mix ingredients and hours into the banquet cost.

Revenue, staffing and the cost of getting it wrong differ across the four. Breakfast can go to a party that can plate on time while the banquet kitchen stays on the hotel roster. Staff meals alone can be split out and everything else left as it is. Separate the jobs before choosing who does them.
## What stays with the hotel, and what moves?

Under in-house operation the hotel still sets the menu, the roster and purchasing, and it still carries waste. A complaint at the desk can be corrected the same day. After outsourcing, the daily lever is the contract. The contractor takes a share or a fee, the hotel employs fewer kitchen staff, and it also loses the ease of changing a menu, adding people or stopping a service on the spot. Guests do not read the contract. The restaurant carries the hotel's name. When food safety, waiting time or hygiene fails, they come to the hotel first.
The table below only shows where responsibility sits. It does not show which option earns more.

| Item | Operated in-house | Outsourced |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Menu and product | The hotel sets it and can change it the same day | Follows the contract; without a standard, it follows the contractor's habit |
| Labour and purchasing | The hotel carries wages, waste and suppliers | The contractor carries daily labour and purchasing; the hotel loses the floor record |
| Complaints and food safety | The hotel handles them and is the licensed operator | Guests still come to the hotel; recovery, the right to stop service, and kitchen access belong in the contract |
| Space, equipment and energy | The hotel's assets, paid by the hotel | Who invests, who maintains, and who owns them at the end must be listed separately |
| Fit with rooms and meetings | Extra staff can be added internally | Depends on agreed hours, minimum staffing and default terms; an added meeting has to be agreed first |
## Which hotels should keep the critical meal periods?

If guests come for the food, do not outsource that meal period first. A resort restaurant, a hotel that keeps guests with local cooking, or a dining room whose name already travels: change the crew and guests notice the food and the service before anyone knows whether the room rate will hold.

Where meetings and banquets are the property's main income, the critical kitchen should stay as well. Split service, extra covers and menu changes that sales has already promised often happen hours before the event. A contract priced on a fixed menu and a fixed crew makes every added meeting a question of whether the contract allows it.

Two other cases are not worth handing over for convenience. If a brand or management agreement already sets product, supplier and staffing standards, and the contractor cannot meet them or will not allow the hotel into the kitchen, outsourcing only moves the miss from the crew into a contract. If the kitchen crew is already stable and outsourcing does not remove people, only adds a share, there is no reason to change who cooks.
## Which hotels can hand one piece over?

Where food is only a guest amenity and the hotel has no stable chefs or purchasing, breakfast or a single meal period can go to a party that can deliver on time. The condition is that the weakness is product and roster, not that this piece is holding up rooms or meetings. Hand over the piece that is holding them up, and both the included breakfast and the meeting offer get worse without the accounts showing it at once.

Staff meals are the clearest piece to separate from the banquet kitchen, either as a fixed staff meal or as a separate contract. They carry no guest experience. Keep feeding them from banquet labour and ingredients, and the banquet loss never becomes readable.

One piece can be outsourced only when three things are visible together: the agreed hours and menu can be delivered; someone holds the food-business licence and the hotel can inspect; the hotel keeps the right to stop the service and to replace the contractor. Miss one, and a low quote only means a smaller fee. It does not mean the risk has left the property.
## Why is a restaurant loss, or a low quote, not enough?

A loss on the restaurant account needs to be put back in the right place first. If breakfast is included in the room rate, revenue sits in rooms and cost sits in food and beverage, so the restaurant will show a loss. If banquet-room depreciation sits in rooms, the kitchen looks worse than it is. After each meal period carries its own items, a real in-house problem is too many people, high ingredient waste, or unstable plating.

Take the quote apart the same way. Beyond the fee or the share, the hotel often still pays for space, energy, equipment upkeep, staff meals, how breakfast vouchers are settled, any banquet minimum, how many people stay on in the low season, who pays when a food-safety incident happens, and who places the staff if the contract ends early. Comparing the quote with today's wages treats those continuing costs as money already saved.

Compare like with like. Keep breakfast, all-day dining, banquets and staff meals separate, and for each one write down where revenue is recorded, who pays labour and ingredients, who pays energy and equipment, and who carries complaints and compensation. If one line does not match, do not switch the whole department.
## Which contract terms, if missing, lose control on the floor?

The contract has to be usable in the kitchen that day. A promise to "ensure quality" cannot be executed. Write down the point at which product can be taken off sale; the hours of service and the minimum crew at check-in peaks and meeting peaks; hygiene, licences and insurance, and who settles the guest and who pays if a food-safety incident occurs; which ingredients must come from named suppliers; who owns the equipment, who maintains it, and how it is handed over when the contract ends; whose employee the cook is, and who places people if the contract is terminated; how often accounts are settled, whether there is a minimum, and how energy is split; whether the hotel may enter the kitchen, and at what point it may end the contract early.

There is no set of figures to copy. How high a minimum should be, and who pays for energy, depends on whether the piece is a guest amenity or a public restaurant. A promise that never enters the contract is not carried out after opening.

In-house operation is not safer merely because that paper is skipped. Someone still has to look, each day, at ingredient prices, how much each meal period produced, and whether complaints point to the food, the wait, or hygiene. Without that daily record, in-house operation only keeps the loss under the department's name.
## What should you check in the current restaurant before deciding?

Check five things first. Can revenue and direct cost for breakfast, all-day dining, banquets and staff meals be recorded separately today? Of recent complaints, how many point to product, waiting and hygiene, and how many are really about the room rate? Do the chefs and the back of house exist mainly for breakfast? Does the brand or management agreement restrict outsourcing or require written consent first? Whose name is on the food-business licence, and whose asset record lists the kitchen equipment?

If any one of the five does not match, fix the record or read the contract before signing an outsourcing agreement. For a piece that can already be separated, trial one meal period and watch three things: whether the product holds, whether extra people can be added at the peak, and who receives the complaint. When that period holds, decide the rest. Do not hand breakfast, banquets and staff meals over on the same day.

If the trial shows unstable product, no way to add people at the peak, or guests still coming to the hotel when the contract has no right to stop the service, stop that meal period. Do not hand over the rest with it. Stopping is not the same as leaving the books as they were: separate the accounts that are still mixed, then decide the next piece.

Fill the table from both sides. The owner decides which piece stays, which piece goes, and how far the minimum, the energy split and early termination are written. The general manager or the food and beverage lead brings the meal-period accounts, whether the crew can plate on time, and where complaints point. They do not sign in place of the owner. If a brand or management company holds the product standard, get the written consent the contract requires before outsourcing. A kitchen report of a loss is information. It is not the owner's approval to outsource.

MarvelBros C&T (迈创兄弟C&T) can put in-house operation and outsourcing on one table for a single hotel, using its meal periods, contracts and back-of-house setup. The table shows which piece should stay and which piece can go. It does not make the decision for the owner.
